# Survival movement attributes and position-evidence boundary

The own-player projection now retains movement speed, gravity, jump strength,
step height, movement efficiency, sneaking speed, safe-fall distance and
fall-damage multiplier. Each is absent until native initialization or a received
update and preserves that basis. A typed Rust definition table routes all twelve
supported own-player attributes, including the four existing stationary/mining
ones. Field routing no longer depends on a numeric list index.

The [native fixture](../data/java_1_21_11/survival_movement.json) and
[provenance](../data/java_1_21_11/survival_movement_source.json) were generated by
`VerifySurvivalMovement.java` against the existing unchanged-body 1.21.11 oracle.
All eight native definitions are tracked attributes. Movement speed and jump
strength defaults preserve their native float-to-double values, not rounded
0.1/0.42 replacements. Native negative gravity and safe-fall values are preserved;
they do not authorize an ordinary construction path. Received modifier evaluation
uses the shared decoder and the corresponding native limits. Truncated batches
are atomic, another entity cannot update these fields, world reset restores
native initialization and reconfiguration clears the projection.

This provides inputs to a future motion model. It does not send survival movement
or claim walking, collision, jumping or arrival acceptance. Tests cover the native
definitions, field routing, limits, modifier application and reset/packet scopes.

## Concern found before connecting locomotion

The current stationary construction context requires a received own position and
zero resolved packet velocity. Creative local movement marks its position as a
submission. Extending that sender with walking alone would leave ordinary
construction blocked after a normal successful walk. Flipping the receive flag
or zeroing the received velocity would falsely relabel predicted state.

Native `ServerPlayNetworkHandler.onPlayerMove` updates the accepted player pose
and tracking state on its ordinary success branch without returning an own-player
position receipt for every step. Its rejection/correction branches can call
`requestTeleport`. Neither elapsed time nor absence of a correction certifies a
specific movement result. This is native source inspection, not a new live trial.

The independent player tracker is also insufficient as a drop-in motion receipt:
its single spatial sequence advances on rotations and metadata, relative moves
are quantized to 1/4096, and it discards received ground bits and sync-position
velocity. A newer viewpoint observation cannot be called a fresh stopped-position
acknowledgement. Native client directional input handling additionally differs
from the 1.16.1 donor and must be compared before reusing its algorithm.

Following the user's instruction to stop when concerns arise, no movement sender,
post-walk construction release, independent arrival authority or live movement
trial has been implemented. The concrete next slice is to separate received pose,
local motion prediction and independent arrival evidence as explicit types,
then connect bounded walk/stop/jump/collision and standing admission through those
types. The current stationary gate remains intact. No MOD, operator command,
teleport fallback or broad entity simulation has been selected as a requirement.
